title: Enforcement Decree of the Dietary Education Support Act
full_text:
Enforcement Decree of the Dietary Education Support Act

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Dietary Education Support Act and matters necessary for its enforcement.

Article 2 (Formulation of Master Plans for Dietary Education)
"Matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 14 (2) 7 of the Dietary Education Support Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") means the following matters: <Amended on March 23, 2013>
1. Matters concerning the establishment of a system for promoting dietary education;
2. Matters concerning the training of personnel specializing in dietary education;
3. Matters concerning the provision of information related to dietary habits;
4. Other matters the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs deems necessary for dietary education.

Article 3 (Evaluation of Performance in Promoting Dietary Education, etc.)
(1) When evaluating performance in promoting dietary education under Article 17 of the Act, the State and local governments shall base their evaluation on the implementation performance of the master plan for dietary education under Article 14 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "master plan"), the Si/Do dietary education plans under Article 16 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "Si/Do plans"), and the Si/Gun/Gu dietary education plans under that Article (hereinafter referred to as "Si/Gun/Gu plans").
(2) To conduct an evaluation under paragraph (1), the State and local governments shall formulate a plan for self-evaluation of performance in promoting dietary education.
(3) The criteria for evaluating performance in promoting dietary education under paragraph (1) shall be as follows: <Amended on March 23, 2013>
1. Appropriateness of the objectives set;
2. Degree of achievement of objectives;
3. Appropriateness of the implementation system and allocation of financial resources;
4. Appropriateness of projects implemented;
5. Other criteria the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs deems necessary for evaluation.
(4) Where the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs or the head of a local government evaluates performance in promoting dietary education under Article 17 (1) of the Act, the Minister or head shall publicly announce the results, by the applicable method specified in the following subparagraphs, within one month from the date the evaluation is completed: <Newly Inserted on December 14, 2021>
1. The Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs: Publication in the Official Gazette and on the website of the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs;
2. The head of a local government: Publication in the local official gazette and on the website of the local government.

Article 4 (Use of Results of Evaluations of Dietary Education)
(1) The State and local governments shall reflect the results of evaluations under Article 3 when formulating the master plan, Si/Do plans, and Si/Gun/Gu plans.
(2) Based on the results of evaluations under Article 3, the State and local governments may select and commend individuals, organizations, or corporations that have made significant contributions to improving the dietary habits of the people.

Article 5 (Composition of the National Dietary Education Committee, etc.)
(1) Members of the National Dietary Education Committee under Article 18 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "National Committee") shall be the following persons: <Amended on March 15, 2010; January 25, 2012; May 22, 2012; March 23, 2013; November 19, 2014; July 26, 2017; October 1, 2025; December 23, 2025; December 30, 2025>
1. The Vice Minister of Finance and Economy, Vice Minister of Education, Vice Minister of the Interior and Safety, Vice Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism, Vice Minister of Health and Welfare, Vice Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment, Vice Minister of Gender Equality and Family, Vice Minister of Oceans and Fisheries, Vice Minister of Planning and Budget, Administrator of the Rural Development Administration, and Minister of Food and Drug Safety. In this case, for an agency with more than one vice minister, the vice minister designated by the head of that agency shall serve as a member;
2. The head of the National Agricultural Cooperative Federation under the Agricultural Cooperatives Act, the head of the National Federation of Fisheries Cooperatives under the Fisheries Cooperatives Act, the head of the National Forestry Cooperative Federation under the Forestry Cooperatives Act, the head of the Korea Rural Economic Institute under the Act on the Establishment, Operation and Fostering of Government-Funded Research Institutes, the head of the Korea Agro-Fisheries and Food Trade Corporation under the Korea Agro-Fisheries and Food Trade Corporation Act, and the head of the Korea Food Research Institute under the Act on the Establishment, Operation and Fostering of Government-Funded Science and Technology Research Institutes;
3. Persons commissioned by the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs, taking gender into consideration, from among the following persons. In this case, persons falling under item (c) shall be included:
(a) Persons who hold or have held positions as school heads, professors, research fellows, or higher-level positions at schools, research institutes, or international organizations related to dietary education;
(b) Persons who have worked or previously worked for at least five years in organizations, administrative agencies, businesses, etc. related to dietary education;
(c) Persons with extensive knowledge and experience in dietary education who are recommended by the respective consultative bodies established under Article 182 (1) 1 and 3 of the Local Autonomy Act.
(2) The term of office of members under paragraph (1) 3 shall be three years.

Article 6 (Duties of Chairpersons)
(1) Each chairperson of the National Committee under Article 18 (4) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "co-chairperson") shall represent the National Committee and exercise overall control over its affairs.
(2) Where both co-chairpersons are unable to perform their duties for an unavoidable reason, a member designated in advance by the chairperson who is the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs shall act on their behalf. <Amended on March 23, 2013>

Article 7 (Meetings)
(1) The co-chairpersons shall convene and preside over meetings of the National Committee.
(2) A meeting of the National Committee shall be convened with the attendance of a majority of all incumbent members, and a resolution shall be adopted with the affirmative vote of a majority of the members present.
(3) Where the National Committee deems it necessary in connection with matters for deliberation, it may have relevant experts attend a meeting to hear their opinions.

Article 8 (Executive Secretary)
(1) The National Committee shall have one executive secretary to handle its administrative affairs.
(2) The executive secretary shall be designated by the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs from among public officials of the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs. <Amended on March 23, 2013>
(3) The executive secretary shall handle the administrative affairs of the National Committee and prepare meeting minutes under the direction of the co-chairpersons.

Article 9 (Allowances, etc.)
Members and other persons attending meetings of the National Committee may be paid allowances and travel expenses within budgetary limits: Provided, That this shall not apply where a member who is a public official attends a meeting of the National Committee in direct connection with the duties under the member's jurisdiction.

Article 10 (Detailed Operating Rules)
Matters necessary for the operation of the National Committee, other than those prescribed in this Decree, shall be determined by the co-chairpersons following a resolution of the National Committee.

Article 10-2 (National Dietary Education Working Committee)
(1) The National Committee shall have a National Dietary Education Working Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Working Committee") to review and coordinate, at the working level, matters to be deliberated on by the National Committee.
(2) The Working Committee shall consist of no more than 20 working members, including one chairperson of the Working Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "working chairperson").
(3) The working chairperson shall be a person designated by the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs from among public officials of the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs who belong to the Senior Executive Service, and the working members shall be the following persons: <Amended on October 1, 2025; December 30, 2025>
1. One person each designated by the head of the relevant agency from among director-level public officials of the Ministry of Finance and Economy, Ministry of Education, Ministry of the Interior and Safety, Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, Ministry of Health and Welfare, Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment, Ministry of Gender Equality and Family, Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, Ministry of Planning and Budget, Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, and Rural Development Administration;
2. Persons commissioned by the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs, taking gender into consideration, from among persons with extensive knowledge and experience in dietary education.
(4) The term of office of working members commissioned under paragraph (3) 2 shall be three years.
(5) Articles 6, 7, and 9 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the operation, etc. of the Working Committee. In such cases, "National Committee" shall be construed as "Working Committee," "co-chairperson" as "working chairperson," and "member" as "working member."
(6) Matters necessary for the operation, etc. of the Working Committee, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (5), shall be determined by the co-chairpersons following a resolution of the National Committee.

Article 11 (Timing, Methods, etc. of Dietary Surveys)
(1) Dietary surveys under Article 21(1) of the Act shall be conducted every three years.
(2) Surveys under paragraph (1) shall be conducted by age, income, and region, using methods such as field surveys, postal surveys, and surveys of statistics and literature.
(3) The Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs may commission a relevant specialized institution or organization to conduct a survey under paragraph (1) to ensure that the survey is conducted efficiently. <Amended on 2013.3.23>
(4) Matters necessary for dietary surveys, other than those provided for in paragraphs (1) through (3), shall be prescribed by the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs. <Amended on 2013.3.23>

Article 12 (Main Contents and Publication Cycle of Dietary Guidelines)
(1) The main contents of the dietary guidelines under Article 22(1) of the Act shall be as follows:
1. Matters concerning the practice of a sound dietary culture;
2. Matters concerning the succession and development of traditional dietary culture;
3. Matters concerning the use of agricultural and fishery products or traditional foods;
4. Matters concerning the consumption of environmentally friendly foods;
5. Other matters necessary for dietary education.
(2) In principle, the dietary guidelines under paragraph (1) shall be published every five years, but the publication cycle may be adjusted where necessary.

Article 13 (Designation of Excellent Rural and Fishing Village Dietary Experience Facilities)
(1) Any person seeking designation as an excellent rural and fishing village dietary experience facility under Article 24(2) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an "excellent experience facility") shall submit an application for designation as an excellent experience facility in attached Form No. 1, accompanied by the following documents, to the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si/Gun/Gu (the head of a Gu means the head of an autonomous Gu; hereinafter referred to as the "head of a Si/Gun/Gu"). <Amended on 2017.11.7>
1. An operational plan;
2. Details of the experience environment, including rural and fishing village dietary experience facilities, the surrounding landscape, and accessibility;
3. A rural and fishing village dietary experience program;
4. Details of personnel engaged in rural and fishing village dietary experience activities or education.
(2) Upon receiving the application documents for designation under paragraph (1), the head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall verify the facts stated in the application through a field survey or other means, and shall then submit the application documents for designation, accompanied by a written opinion on whether the designation criteria under Article 24(3) of the Act are met, to the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs through the Special Metropolitan City Mayor, Metropolitan City Mayor, or Do Governor. In such cases, the Special Self-Governing City Mayor or Special Self-Governing Province Governor shall submit them directly to the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs. <Amended on 2013.3.23, 2017.11.7>
(3) Upon receiving the application documents for designation and the written opinion under paragraph (2), the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs shall review whether the designation criteria under Article 24(3) of the Act are met and, if the Minister finds that they are met, shall designate the facility as an excellent experience facility. <Amended on 2013.3.23>
(4) Where the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs designates an excellent experience facility under paragraph (3), the Minister shall issue a certificate of designation as an excellent experience facility in attached Form No. 2. <Amended on 2013.3.23>

Article 14 (Designation of Dietary Education Institutions)
(1) Any person seeking designation as a dietary education institution under Article 25(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "dietary education institution") shall submit an application for designation as a dietary education institution in attached Form No. 3, accompanied by the following documents, to the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs. <Amended on 2013.3.23>
1. An operational plan;
2. The curriculum and educational content;
3. Details of personnel engaged in education;
4. Details of the educational environment established, including facilities and equipment.
(2) Upon receiving the application documents for designation under paragraph (1), the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs shall review whether the designation criteria under Article 25(2) of the Act are met and, if the Minister finds that they are met, shall designate the institution as a dietary education institution. <Amended on 2013.3.23>
(3) Where the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs designates a dietary education institution under paragraph (2), the Minister shall issue a certificate of designation as a dietary education institution in attached Form No. 4. <Amended on 2013.3.23>

Article 14-2 (Designation of Dietary Education Support Centers, etc.)
(1) Deleted. <2017.11.7>
(2) An institution or organization seeking designation as a dietary education support center under Article 25-2(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "support center") shall submit an application for designation as a dietary education support center in attached Form No. 5 (including an application in electronic form), accompanied by the following documents (including electronic documents), to the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs or the head of a local government. <Amended on 2013.3.23, 2017.11.7>
1. Its articles of incorporation;
2. Details of its dedicated personnel and organizational structure;
3. A business plan for the activities specified in the subparagraphs of Article 25-2(3) of the Act.
(3) The Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs or the head of a local government who receives an application under paragraph (2) shall verify the certificate of corporate registration through the joint use of administrative information under Article 36(1) of the Electronic Government Act. <Amended on 2013.3.23>
(4) Where the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs or the head of a local government receives an application for designation under paragraph (2), the Minister or the head of the local government shall evaluate whether the designation criteria under Article 25-2(2) of the Act are met after hearing the opinions of relevant experts and, if the Minister or the head of the local government finds that they are met, may designate the institution or organization as a support center. <Amended on 2013.3.23, 2017.11.7>
(5) Where the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs or the head of a local government designates a support center under paragraph (4), the Minister or the head of the local government shall issue a certificate of designation as a dietary education support center in attached Form No. 6. <Amended on 2013.3.23>
(6) An institution or organization designated as a support center shall submit the results of its activities for the preceding year and its business plan for the relevant year to the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs or the head of a local government by the last day of February each year. <Amended on 2013.3.23>
(7) Deleted. <2017.11.7>
(8) Matters necessary for the procedures for designation and the operation of support centers, other than those provided for in paragraphs (1) through (6), shall be prescribed by the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs. <Amended on 2013.3.23, 2017.11.7>

Article 15 (Policy Measures to Promote Community Dietary Education)
"Policy measures prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as the development and dissemination of community dietary education programs and support for necessary expenses" in Article 26-2 of the Act means the following:
1. Development and dissemination of community dietary education programs;
2. Operation of community dietary education courses;
3. Support for expenses necessary for community dietary education;
4. Other matters that the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs determines to be necessary for community dietary education. In such cases, a local government may prescribe additional policy measures by ordinance of the relevant local government, taking into account local circumstances and other factors.

Article 16 (Dietary Education Week)
(1) Pursuant to Article 26-3 of the Act, the one-week period that includes September 11 of each year shall be Dietary Education Week.
(2) The State and local governments may hold events to publicize the importance of sound dietary practices and promote dietary education in commemoration of Dietary Education Week under paragraph (1).
